findings.title: Caller-controlled string reaches a shell
findings.why: The shell parses the string, so everything in it is syntax: `;`, `&&`, `$()` and backticks all run. When the caller writes that string, the caller is writing code, and the tool description is the only boundary.
findings.fix: Either validate against an allowlist that matches the whole command and fails closed, or move to `execFile` with an argv array so nothing is parsed.

findings.title: Joins caller-supplied paths without a containment check
findings.why: `path.join(ROOT, args.path)` looks confined but is not: `../../etc/passwd` walks straight out of ROOT, and an absolute segment discards the prefix entirely. The model writes that string, and so does anything else that can call the tool.
findings.fix: Resolve, then compare with a separator: `const p = path.resolve(ROOT, input); if (!p.startsWith(ROOT + path.sep)) throw`. On Windows use `path.relative` and reject a leading `..`.

findings.title: Can write or mutate files and state
findings.why: Read-plus-write is where mistakes become damage. Note whether writes are confined and whether they are reversible.
findings.fix: Confine write roots, and prefer explicit overwrite semantics over silent replace.

findings.title: Dependency ranges that can float
findings.why: A caret or star range means today’s install and tomorrow’s install can be different code. For a component that holds credentials and runs commands, that is unearned trust.
findings.fix: Pin exact versions, or at minimum commit a lockfile and install with `npm ci`.

findings.title: Package runs code at install time
findings.why: preinstall/install/postinstall executes before you have run anything, with your user permissions. This is the standard vector for a compromised dependency.
findings.fix: Read the script. Pin the version and check it has no network access.

findings.title: Uses stdio transport
findings.why: Local stdio servers inherit your user account. There is no sandbox between the server and your files.
findings.fix: Prefer stdio for local work and HTTP with auth for remote.

findings.title: Capability declaration does not match what the server serves
findings.why: The capabilities block is the contract the host negotiates with. Declaring `tools: {}` and then answering `tools/list` means the client never agreed to tools, so list-change notifications go nowhere and some hosts keep a stale catalog. The reverse — advertising tools with no `tools/call` handler — gives the model a catalog it cannot invoke.
findings.fix: Declare what the server really serves: `capabilities: { tools: { listChanged: true } }`, and implement every tool listed.
findings.detail: inconclusive: registration is dynamic, read it by hand
